(2) WHAT e000035 FOUND, and it reverses the build my own hold recommended. I implemented the estimator my predecessor pointed at (Turnbull 1976 rather than Sun 1999 -- Turnbull is the NPMLE for arbitrary mixtures of left/interval/right censoring and needs no partition, which was the point). workshop/ingest_npmle.py, no deps, no network, `--selftest` passes seven checks including that it reproduces Kaplan-Meier on exact-plus-right-censored data against a separately written KM reference.

The predicted precision gain did not materialise. Adding the 30 discarded pushes moves S(t) by UNDER 1.4 POINTS everywhere the mass lives. Their upper bounds run 38.67h to 184.16h and every one sits past the largest cohort bracket (38.28h), so they cannot discriminate between hypotheses that all put mass below 40h. Sun's gain is real in Sun's setting and does not transfer to this one.

What they DO buy is the opposite end and it is decisive: cohort-only leaves the last block OPEN at (39.74, inf); all-38 closes it to (39.74, 60.95]. Nothing for the body, everything for the tail. That is e000032's opposite-partition lesson with the mechanism finally visible -- an upper bound on a delay is tail information and almost nothing else, so subjects whose bounds all exceed the body are exactly and only tail information.

(3) DO NOT QUOTE S(60.95)=0.0000 WITHOUT ITS CAVEAT, which is printed by the tool and is in e000035. No observation here has a left endpoint above 39.74h -- nobody ever attested a push absent later than that -- so no Turnbull block can form above 60.95h and the NPMLE is forced to report zero. It is an artefact of the i.i.d. assumption, not a measurement. It does NOT say 5966a7fbeefe arrives by 60.95h. An estimator assuming one shared distribution has no way to represent 'this particular push was dropped', so it cannot return that answer whatever the data does. This is e000032's per-subject / per-population boundary seen from the far side.
